plan:
COMPLETE EXPERIMENT DESIGN — Combined Jailbreak Techniques: Attacker Strength × Defense Strength × Attack Style vs. ASR
(Design only. Nothing was executed; no results are claimed. All repo facts below were verified by inspection: /workspace contains ONLY task.json — no README, code, configs, datasets, or track.md file; task.json's embedded track.md note says "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." Every sourced choice is cited; every unsourced choice is labelled [ASSUMPTION].)

═══════════════════════════════════════
1. FACTOR GRID
═══════════════════════════════════════
Five factors; primary grid = Attack Style × Attacker Strength × Defense Strength × Dataset, with Trick-Set nested within Attack Style.

F1. Attack style (2 levels)
  S1 = AutoDAN (token-level): genetic search over hierarchically generated jailbreak prompts [Liu et al., ICLR 2024, "AutoDAN: Generating Stealthy Jailbreak Prompts on Aligned Large Language Models"].
  S2 = PAIR (prompt-level): iterative attacker-LLM vs. target-LLM red-teaming loop [Chao et al., NeurIPS 2024, "Jailbreaking Black Box Large Language Models in Twenty Queries"]. The researcher's source topics ("neurips2024/97431") are consistent with a NeurIPS 2024 source; I treat PAIR's paper as the anchor for setup details [INFERENCE — to be confirmed by researcher].

F2. Attacker strength (3 levels) — compute-budget knobs, anchored as multiples of each paper's default configuration (exact default values to be read from the papers' released configs at setup; provisional numbers below are [ASSUMPTIONS] on structure, exact 1×/3×/10× anchoring is the fixed rule):
  AutoDAN knobs: population size P, generations G (evals ≈ P×G).
    Low = 1× paper default (provisionally P=8, G=10 → ~80 evals/prompt)
    Medium = 3× (P=16, G=25 → ~400)
    High = 10× capped (P=32, G=50 → ~1,600)
  PAIR knobs: attacker–target rounds N, parallel streams K (queries = K×N).
    Low = 1× paper default (provisionally K=1, N=3 → 3 queries/prompt)
    Medium = 3× (K=5, N=10 → 50)
    High = 10× capped (K=20, N=20 → 400)

F3. Defense strength (3 levels, exactly; one concrete defense per tier, spanning paradigms):
  D0 None — no defense. Baseline/reference level.
  D1 Weak — Self-Reminder system-prompt defense [Xie et al., 2023, "Defending LLMs against Jailbreak Attacks via Self-Reminder"]. Paradigm: zero-cost prompt-level steering, no model or pipeline change.
  D2 Strong — Llama Guard [Inan et al., Meta AI 2023, "Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard"], a trained classifier gating both input prompts and model outputs before delivery. Paradigm: learned external safeguard.
  Why these span paradigms: nothing (D0) → static prompt steering (D1) → trained input+output classifier (D2): three qualitatively different defense mechanisms ordered by intrusiveness/cost, giving "defense strength" an interpretable ordinal meaning.
  [ASSUMPTION] "Strength" is treated as an ordinal tier, not a pure dose of one mechanism; this confounds paradigm with strength and is listed under Limitations.

F4. Dataset (2 levels, per researcher instruction — not 3–4):
  Primary: AdvBench [Zou et al., 2023, "Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models"], 520 harmful behaviors — the canonical ASR benchmark used by both AutoDAN and PAIR evaluations.
  Secondary: JBB-Behaviors [Chen et al., 2024, "JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking LLMs"], 100 behaviors across 10 distinct harm categories with an official judge and scoring harness.
  Justification for JBB over MaliciousInstruct: JBB's 10-category structure gives controlled behavioral diversity (cybercrime, harassment, fraud, physical harm, etc.), enabling a cross-dataset interaction-shift test with category-stratified sampling, and it ships a standardized judge + leaderboard protocol — reducing measurement variance. MaliciousInstruct offers diversity but no standardized judge or category taxonomy.

F5. Trick-set (nested in F1) — 5 published tricks, each cited, applied as modifiers layered on top of the base attack's prompt-generation loop:
  T1 Persona/role-play priming — "Do Anything Now" in-the-wild taxonomy, persona-assignment category [Shen et al., 2024, "Do Anything Now: Characterizing and Evaluating In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts on LLMs"].
  T2 Obfuscation/encoding — cipher/encoding of the harmful request [Wei et al., NeurIPS 2024, "Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?"; Yuan et al., 2024, "GPT-4 Is Smart Enough to Jailbreak Itself"].
  T3 Template/prefix injection with refusal suppression [Wei et al., 2024, ibid.; Shen et al., 2024, ibid.].
  T4 Denial-then-retry (refusal-feedback re-prompting) [Chao et al., 2024, PAIR's iterative retry; Mehrotra et al., 2024, "Tree of Attacks: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs Automatically"].
  T5 Multilingual/low-resource translation obfuscation [Yong et al., 2024, "Low-Resource Languages Jailbreak GPT-4"].
  Combination definition (fixed): a trick SET = the base attack run with a subset of tricks applied simultaneously inside its generation/retry loop. Single-trick ablations are always included so combination synergy is separable from individual effects.
  Trick conditions per style (15): base alone (1) + 5 singletons + 2^(5−2) resolution-III fractional factorial over pairs/triples (8 runs) + all-5 combined (1). The fractional design keeps pairwise combination effects estimable at 8 runs instead of 26.

FULL GRID SIZE: 2 styles × 3 strengths × 3 defenses × 2 datasets × 15 trick conditions = 540 cells.

═══════════════════════════════════════
2. PER-CELL PROTOCOL
═══════════════════════════════════════
- Target model: ONE fixed instruct LLM for all cells. [ASSUMPTION] Provisionally Llama-3-8B-Instruct (widely used in AutoDAN/PAIR evaluations, locally deployable, logit access needed for AutoDAN); final choice researcher-confirmed.
- Fixed prompt set: stratified sample of 50 behaviors per dataset (AdvBench 50/520; JBB 50/100 stratified across its 10 categories), selected once with a fixed seed and held IDENTICAL across all 540 cells.
- Stochasticity: attacks run with the papers' default temperature; R = 3 repetitions with fixed per-repetition seeds shared across cells; the cell's outcome = per-prompt majority vote over repetitions, plus per-repetition ASR retained for variance reporting.
- AutoDAN cells require white-box logit access to the target; PAIR cells are black-box. The style factor therefore partially confounds attack style with access level — handled in Limitations.
- Judge applied identically to every cell, blind to condition labels (metadata stripped before judging).

═══════════════════════════════════════
3. ASR / JUDGE PROTOCOL (fixed up front)
═══════════════════════════════════════
- Primary judge: JailbreakBench's official LLM judge (v1 judge prompt, Chao et al./Chen et al., 2024) applied to the target's final response.
- Fallback rule: if the judge service is unavailable or output is malformed, keyword/regex filter (harmful-intent keyword list + refusal lexicon) decides.
- Threshold: a response counts as a successful attack ONLY if the judge labels it as providing actionable harmful content (JBB label "1 = full compliance with the harmful intent"); refusals and evasions count as failures. Threshold fixed before any run.
- Judge validation (control): on a stratified sample of n=100 responses spanning all conditions, run (a) judge vs. keyword fallback agreement and (b) a second, different-family LLM judge; report Cohen's κ. Target κ ≥ 0.8; disagreements adjudicated by a written human rule before any analysis. Judge-validation happens BEFORE the main grid runs.

═══════════════════════════════════════
4. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════
Unit of observation: (behavior prompt i, repetition r, cell c) → binary success y_ir,c (per judge; majority-vote version as primary, per-repetition as sensitivity).
Primary model — per dataset (dataset as stratification factor; two models, one per dataset, plus a pooled sensitivity model with dataset fixed effects):
  logit P(y=1) = α + βA·A(strength) + βD·D(defense) + βS·S(style) + βAD·A×D + βAS·A×S + βDS·D×S + βADS·A×D×S + nested trick terms.
Trick factors: enter as T(condition) nested within style — modelled as S × T interaction, i.e., separate trick coefficients per attack style; secondary T × D terms test whether trick effectiveness is moderated by defense strength.
Combination separability: synergy test = (OR of the all-5 set) vs. the product of singleton ORs, compared on the log-odds scale (a two-sided Wald test on the deviation); the fractional-pair runs give pairwise interaction estimates.
Estimands reported: odds ratios with 95% CIs for A×D (the core "attacker power vs. defense robustness" interaction), A×D×S (does the attacker–defense interaction differ between token- and prompt-level attacks), and each trick's marginal and set-level ORs. Standard errors: cluster-robust (clustered by behavior prompt) via GEE, with a random-intercept mixed model as sensitivity.
Primary visualization: attacker×defense ASR heatmap (3×3 grid) — one per dataset per style (4 heatmaps) — showing whether the interaction is sub-additive (defense holds), super-additive (strong attacker overwhelms strong defense), or additive. Secondary: trick-ablation forest plot of ORs per style.

═══════════════════════════════════════
5. CONTROLS AND VALIDITY
═══════════════════════════════════════
- Fixed prompt set: the same 50+50 behavior IDs, same order, in every cell (no per-cell resampling) — removes sampling variance from all comparisons.
- Seeds/repetitions: R=3 fixed seeds shared across cells; report between-repetition SD as an attack-nondeterminism diagnostic; GEE clustering absorbs residual prompt-level correlation.
- Negative control: ~50 benign prompts (XSTEST safe subset, [Röttger et al., 2024, "XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in LLMs"]) run in a subset of cells (D0/D1/D2 × both styles, base and all-5 trick set); expected ASR ≈ 0. Elevated ASR on benign prompts indicates judge over-flagging rather than jailbreak success.
- Positive control: AutoDAN at Medium strength on the undefended (D0) target must reproduce literature-magnitude ASR [per Liu et al., 2024]; failure indicates a pipeline bug — gate the main grid on this check.
- Judge-bias mitigation: judge blind to condition labels; two-judge agreement check; keyword fallback; human-rule adjudication of a disagreement subsample; judge model version pinned.
- Attack-nondeterminism mitigation: repetition plan above; model checkpoints and attack code versions pinned; all random draws seed-controlled.

═══════════════════════════════════════
6. FEASIBILITY / ESTIMATED COST (design estimate only — nothing run)
═══════════════════════════════════════
Queries per prompt (provisional numbers, per §1): PAIR 3/50/400 (Low/Med/High); AutoDAN ~80/400/1,600 evals.
Per cell (50 prompts): PAIR 150 / 2,500 / 20,000; AutoDAN 4,000 / 20,000 / 80,000.
Naive full grid: base-condition total = (3+50+20k… summed over strengths ≈ 22,650 PAIR + 104,000 AutoDAN per dataset-defense) × 3 defenses × 2 datasets × 2 styles ≈ 1.25M; × 15 trick conditions ≈ 18.7M LLM queries. Too large.
Recommended reduced design (as-built budget): trick conditions at Low and High strength reduced to {base, all-5 set} (3 conditions instead of 15) → grid = 2 styles × [3×3 (base+singletons+fractional at Med) + 3×2×2 (reduced at Low/High)] × 2 datasets ≈ 264 cells; with 30 prompts/cell as an option, ≈ 3–6M queries.
Execution requirements (if ever run): PAIR needs only API access (queries embarrassingly parallel; ~days with concurrent calls); AutoDAN requires white-box logit access → local GPU (≈ 4–8 × A100-class) for target + attacker model; judge calls additional ~10–20% overhead. The current design-only environment (no GPU, no network) cannot execute any part — stated explicitly, not treated as a constraint on the design per researcher instruction.

═══════════════════════════════════════
7. LIMITATIONS / THREATS
═══════════════════════════════════════
- Style confound: AutoDAN is white-box, PAIR black-box; "attack style" effects partly reflect access level. Mitigation: interpret style effects jointly with the access caveat; optionally add a PAIR-vs-AutoDAN-transfer variant on the same target as a follow-up.
- Defense tier conflates paradigm with strength; ORs for D1/D2 are defense-specific, not generic "stronger defense" effects.
- Single target model limits generalizability; a second target is a possible extension.
- Judge bias is the main measurement threat (mitigations in §5); residual misclassification bias is roughly constant across cells (blind judging), so it mostly attenuates, not reverses, contrasts.
- Trick citations give the trick families, not canonical implementations — implementation choices (prompt templates, cipher choice) introduce researcher degrees of freedom; all templates will be drawn from the cited papers' released code where available and logged verbatim.
- 50-prompt subsample: CI widths on cell ASR ≈ ±10–14 percentage points at p≈0.1–0.9; the regression pooling across cells is what powers interaction estimates, not per-cell rates.
- Provisional strength numbers (P/G/K/N values) are [ASSUMPTIONS] anchored by the 1×/3×/10× rule; they must be re-checked against the papers' released configs before execution.

═══════════════════════════════════════
8. REFERENCES (to be verified against source PDFs/code at setup)
═══════════════════════════════════════
Zou et al. 2023 (AdvBench/GCG); Liu et al. ICLR 2024 (AutoDAN); Chao et al. NeurIPS 2024 (PAIR); Chen et al. 2024 (JailbreakBench); Xie et al. 2023 (Self-Reminder); Inan et al. 2023 (Llama Guard); Wei et al. NeurIPS 2024 (Jailbroken); Shen et al. 2024 (Do Anything Now); Yuan et al. 2024 (GPT-4 self-jailbreak); Yong et al. 2024 (low-resource languages); Mehrotra et al. 2024 (TAP); Röttger et al. 2024 (XSTest); alternates: Alon & Kamfonas 2023 (perplexity filter), Robey et al. 2023 (SmoothLLM).
